title: Tenant SNAT port shadowing after LB HA failover leads to cross-tenant DNS misassociation
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: During a dedicated-customer incident we observed DNS responses being attributed to the wrong tenant following an active/passive LB failover. Affected customers saw transient DNS resolution failures and unexpected connection resets. This ticket captures investigation, mitigation, and a durable fix to prevent SNAT port reuse and conntrack mismatch from causing cross-tenant response attribution.

Symptoms and impact:
- Multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent DNS failures and 5xx errors from services that rely on internal name resolution (customer escalations opened between 2026-03-05 and 2026-03-06).
- Packet traces from two clusters show DNS replies arriving with source ports that matched ephemeral SNAT ports recently used by a different tenant. Because conntrack entries expired on the original host after LB failover, replies were mapped to the wrong socket on the receiving node.
- Scope: 3 clusters, ~12 affected tenant endpoints sporadically over 36 hours. P95 latency spikes and a small number of request-level errors.

Reproduction notes:
1) Create two tenants sharing the same SNAT range with ephemeral port allocation.
2) Initiate high-rate UDP (DNS) queries from tenant A and tenant B through the same outbound LB.
3) Force an LB node active/standby failover (simulate HA switchover) while conntrack entries on the new path have shorter timeouts.
4) Observe DNS replies that arrive on the new path being matched to existing sockets belonging to the other tenant when ephemeral ports collide.

Root cause analysis:
- Load balancer HA failover causes flows to transit a new egress host. That host had different conntrack timeout tuning and reused ephemeral SNAT ports from a recent tenant, creating port collisions.
- Conntrack entries for DNS (UDP) are short-lived on the failover target due to a local kernel tuning change and a bug in our conntrack reconciliation code that skipped some tenant namespaces during a rapid sync.
- Combined effect: UDP responses are accepted and forwarded to the wrong tenant socket, producing DNS misassociations.

Immediate mitigations applied: (2026-03-07)
- Emergency runbook step added to clear conntrack entries for affected egress host: sudo conntrack -D --orig-port-dst=53 (applied in targeted clusters).
- Applied temporary per-tenant deterministic SNAT port padding to minimize immediate collisions for high-rate customers.
- Added a temporary egress ACL to isolate tenants with known symptoms while root cause fix is developed.

Proposed durable fixes:
1) Deterministic per-tenant SNAT port ranges: reserve distinct ephemeral port sub-ranges per tenant to eliminate cross-tenant port reuse on the same host.
2) Conntrack sync hardening: fix reconciliation logic to ensure tenant namespaces are always included during rapid state sync and align conntrack timeouts across the fleet (net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_udp_timeout).
3) HA switchover path validation: add a short-term blackhole/validation handshake on failover paths for UDP flows to ensure conntrack priming before allowing responses through to tenant veths.
4) Observability: add a dedicated metric that counts "udp-snat-collisions" when a received flow matches an existing conntrack entry with a different tenant id; surface in Console alerts and per-tenant dashboards.

Implementation plan and rollout:
- Patch 1 (conntrack sync + timeout alignment) targeted for runtime-1.26 hotfix. QA on staging (two days) -> Canary to 10% multi-tenant clusters -> full fleet. Estimated 3 days dev + 2 days canary.
- Patch 2 (per-tenant SNAT port allocator) is more intrusive (changes in egress agent). Implement as opt-in feature flag, test for portability across kernels, then gradually enable for high-risk tenants. Estimated 2 sprints.
- Patch 3 (failover handshake) implemented as a short code path in LB agent; targeted canary after Patch 1.

Acceptance criteria:
- No DNS cross-tenant misassociation in canary clusters for 72h under simulated HA failovers.
- Metric "udp-snat-collisions" drops to zero in canaries and does not spike on gradual rollout.
- Regression tests added to networking CI that simulate failovers and verify tenant-level isolation remains intact.

Rollout notes and rollback plan:
- Each change will be feature-flagged. Rollout proceeds cluster-by-cluster with runbook steps to rollback by disabling flag and applying conntrack clear if anomalies appear.

Stakeholders and communications:
- Escalation owners: Lina Chen (SRE) and Diego Ramos (Networking Eng).
- Notified customers: Customer A, Customer B, Customer C — customer success notified and provided mitigation steps.
- Public incident postmortem to be drafted in Confluence after post-incident review.
comments: 2026-03-07: Initial triage - Lina Chen gathered tcpdump traces and confirmed port collisions. Temporary conntrack flush and per-tenant SNAT padding applied; customer-facing mitigations shared.
2026-03-09: Diego implemented a failing-unit test that reproduces port collision locally; working on conntrack reconciliation patch.
2026-03-11: PR #4892 opened for conntrack sync fix and timeout alignment. Awaiting code review from @michael and @sana.
2026-03-12: Added UDP collision metric to canary ingest via Console. First canary showed 0->2 collisions during a synthetic HA test; investigating residual spacing issue.
2026-03-14: Removed temporary egress ACL for isolated tenant after confirmed reduced collision rate in canaries; still in In Progress for full rollout.
Reviewer feedback: please add automated CI scenario for LB failovers and include kernel-version matrix in the PR description.
next_steps: Finish code review for PR #4892, add kernel matrix tests, schedule canary for conntrack patch next maintenance window, and start design for per-tenant SNAT allocator (design doc in Confluence).
notes_for_oncall: If customers report DNS misassociation after deployments, immediately run conntrack clear on target host and set the per-tenant SNAT padding flag. Check udp-snat-collisions metric; if >0, roll back recent flags and open ENG-74521 with updates.
